# Full Page Shot

> A Microsoft Edge extension and MCP server that captures entire web pages (full scroll, any length) as PNG/JPEG. Written in TypeScript, bundled with esbuild. Used by humans and AI agents.

Full Page Shot captures full-page screenshots via the Chrome DevTools Protocol. It handles pages up to 65,000+ px, internal scroll containers, lazy loading, Canvas/WebGL, cookie banners, and more. It also ships an MCP server and CLI so AI agents can capture pages programmatically.

## Quick start (humans)

- Install: `npm run setup` (npm install + build)
- Load `dist/` in Edge (`edge://extensions/` → Developer mode → Load unpacked)
- Click the icon → Capture full page (or `Ctrl+Shift+S`)

## Quick capture (agents)

- CLI: `node tools/agent-capture.mjs <url>` → prints JSON with file path and dimensions
- MCP: register the server (auto-detected via `.mcp.json`), then call `capture_full_page({ url })`
- Auto-launches Chrome if not running

## Tools (MCP / CLI)

- `capture_full_page(url, format?, quality?)` — captures entire page, returns base64 image
- `capture_visible(url?, format?, quality?)` — captures visible viewport only
- `list_tabs()` — lists open tabs
- `navigate(tabId, url)` — navigates a tab
- `browser_status()` — checks if Chrome is ready

## Build & test

- `npm run check` — typecheck + build
- `node tools/smoke-test.mjs --include-segments` — 12 E2E scenarios
- `node tools/verify-clipboard.mjs` — clipboard verification
